native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the hundred-year time-slice PCA on the forms of capital (PC1 ~30% variance; positive PC1 = amber/depot direction), the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) are both characterized by strongly positive PC1, i.e. a profile dominated by social capital (amber, +0.75) and economic capital (depots/hoards, +0.44) against symbolic capital (hatchet/sword, -0.30) and monument count (-0.29). MN PC1 is positive and rising across the phase (mean +1.39, from +0.6 at 3400 to +1.8 at 3000 BCE); YN PC1 is also positive but slightly lower and decaying (mean +1.13, peaking +1.6 at 2800 BCE, dipping at 2700 BCE, falling to +0.4 by 2300 BCE). Both phases sit on the same high-positive pole well above the Late Neolithic (-0.34) and Bronze Age phases (OBA -3.13, YBA -1.87).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/capital.csv (39 hundred-year BCE slices), parsed European decimal commas, standardized the 12 Z-indicators, ran PCA via numpy SVD, sign-fixed PC1 positive = amber/depot direction (amber loading > 0), extracted per-slice PC1, computed MN (3400-3000) and YN/SG (2900-2300) phase statistics and trajectories, reported loadings grouped by the locked four-capital mapping (Symbolic=hatchet/sword+dagger+house size, Social=copper/gold+amber+monument count, Cultural=pottery form+decoration, Economic=depot+sickle+axe/celt+monument size), ran a 4-form-aggregation PCA as a sanity check, and computed a pollen-openness correlation as optional context only.
